# navigera

> navigera is browser automation for AI agents from the shell: one native binary (Rust, no Node) that drives Chrome over the DevTools Protocol, one command per step, with pages read as a compact accessibility tree with [ref=N] handles.

Each page below is markdown. The whole site in one file: https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/llms-full.txt

## Start

- [Install](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/start/install.md): Every way to install navigera, the platforms it runs on, and which browser it uses.
- [Quick start](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/start/quick-start.md): One session and four commands, from install to a page read.
- [A first session](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/start/tutorial.md): A tour of one session: the page tree and its refs, the commands, how to name an element, and what comes back.

## Guides

- [Hand the agent your browser](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/guides/your-browser.md): Give an agent your own signed-in browser, a copy of its profile, or a saved state, and take a step back from it.
- [Drive a browser from a program](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/guides/programs.md): Keep one browser on a pipe with `navigera serve`: one JSON command per line in, one JSON reply per line out.
- [Let a fast model pick the element](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/guides/decider.md): Hand the two small decisions, which element and did it work, to a fast decision model instead of the agent's LLM.
- [Use a page's own tools (WebMCP)](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/guides/webmcp.md): Call the tools a page registers for agents through WebMCP, and see which ones it offers.
- [Switch from agent-browser](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/guides/from-agent-browser.md): agent-browser's commands and flags, each with its navigera equivalent.

## Concepts

- [How navigera works](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/concepts/how-it-works.md): The three ways to run navigera, and what it does for you between the commands: waits, settling, tabs, dialogs.
- [Supported browsers](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/concepts/browsers.md): Which browsers and engines navigera drives, how CI tests each one, and how a browser is found or installed.
- [Several models, one browser](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/concepts/multi-model.md): Why a small decision model sits beside the agent's LLM, what it was measured to do, and what comes next.

## Reference

- [Commands](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/reference/commands.md): Every command, its arguments and flags, and what it prints.
- [navigera --help](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/reference/help.md): The command list exactly as this build prints it.

## Agents

- [For AI agents](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/agents/overview.md): What an agent gets: the skill, the MCP server, and these docs as markdown.
- [Skill](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/agents/skill.md): The guide `navigera install-skill` gives an agent, as this version prints it.
- [Skill references](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/agents/skill-references.md): The detail the skill sends an agent to when a topic comes up: acting, reading, inspecting, sessions, Electron, the decider, setup and errors.
- [MCP server](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/agents/mcp.md): Run navigera as a Model Context Protocol server for IDE agents, with the setup for each client.

## Benchmarks

- [Results](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/benchmarks/results.md): Every driver and agent tool on the same scripted session, from one CI run, with how each number is taken.
- [Where navigera is not ahead](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/benchmarks/losses.md): Each measure on which another tool beat navigera in the same run.
- [Agent eval](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/benchmarks/agent-eval.md): Whether a generic coding agent, given only the tool and its docs, finishes real tasks with navigera, Playwright and agent-browser.

## Project

- [Changelog](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/project/changelog.md): What changed in each release, and what is on the way.
- [Contributing](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/project/contributing.md): How to build, test, benchmark and release navigera.
- [Source layout](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/project/layout.md): Where each part of navigera lives in the repository.
- [Security](https://andrey-usa.github.io/navigera/project/security.md): What navigera protects and how, its known exposures, and how to report a problem.
